hints: Focus on the iodoform test, the yellow precipitate of CHI3 forms only with two specific groups.
Look for a CH3CO group or a CH3CH(OH) group in each structure, compound 2 clearly has CH3CH(OH)CH2OH.
Check compound 1 for ethanal or methyl ketone character and re-examine the right hand end of compound 3 for that same key fragment.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform condition**

This yellow precipitate with alkaline aqueous iodine is the triiodomethane (iodoform) test. It is positive only for two fragments.

$$\text{positive if } \text{CH}_3\text{CO}- \text{ present OR } \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}- \text{ present}$$

**Test compound 1**

Compound 1 has a tertiary alcohol on the left, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C(OH)}-$, which cannot be oxidised, and an aldehyde $-\text{CHO}$ on the right. It is not ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, and it has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group, so it is negative.

**Test compound 2**

Compound 2 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$, propane-1,2-diol. It contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit directly, so alkaline $\text{I}_2$ oxidises it and then cleaves it to give $\text{CHI}_3$. This one is positive.

**Test compound 3 and conclude**

Compound 3 has a tertiary alcohol at one end, which is negative, but the other end is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3\text{)}-$. That is again a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group, so it is also positive. Only 2 and 3 give the yellow precipitate.

options.A: Incorrect. This suggests all three are positive. Compound 1 is the trap, its -CHO is a simple aldehyde, not CH3CHO, and its alcohol is tertiary, so it cannot give CHI3.
options.B: Incorrect. This includes 1 and 2. Compound 2 is correctly included, but compound 1 has no CH3CO- and no CH3CH(OH)- group, so it does not react.
options.C: Correct. Both compound 2, CH3CH(OH)CH2OH, and compound 3, which ends in CH3CH(OH)-, contain the methyl secondary alcohol fragment that is oxidised by alkaline iodine to give yellow CHI3. Compound 1 does not.
options.D: Incorrect. This omits compound 2. Compound 2 is the classic example of a CH3CH(OH)- containing diol and is strongly positive, so any answer without 2 is incomplete.
